title: Adding a Second Story to Your Westchester Home: What You Need to Know
excerpt: A second-story addition can transform your home and give you the space your family needs. Here's what the process really looks like when you work with an architect and builder in Westchester County.
content:
If you're running out of room in your Westchester home, a second-story addition might be exactly what you're looking for. It's one of the smartest ways to add square footage without eating up your yard or moving to a new house. But it's also one of the more complex projects you can undertake, which is why you need the right team.

A second-story addition isn't just about framing walls and adding a roof. It involves structural engineering, permit approvals, and careful planning. That's where having a licensed architect in Westchester, NY who also holds a general contractor license makes all the difference.

Why the Design and Build Team Matters

When one person serves as both architect and general contractor, you avoid a lot of headaches. There's no finger-pointing between two firms. There's no miscommunication between what was designed and what gets built. You get clarity from day one.

Silvio M. Luca runs House Architecture and Construction as a design-build firm, which means he handles both the architectural design and the construction. He's licensed as a New York State architect and as a general contractor. He personally oversees every project, from the initial concept through final completion. Whether you're in Scarsdale, Bronxville, Larchmont, or any other part of Westchester County, this hands-on approach keeps everything moving in the same direction.

Permitting and Local Codes Across Westchester

Every municipality in Westchester has its own building department and permit process. That's just how it works here. Whether your home is in Mamaroneck, Rye, Harrison, or White Plains, you'll need local approval before breaking ground.

This isn't a reason to worry. It's normal. The key is working with someone who understands each town's requirements and has done projects in your area before. A residential architect in Westchester with real local experience knows what inspectors look for and how to get your plans approved efficiently.

Planning Your Second-Story Addition

Before permits and construction crews show up, you need a solid design. That means understanding your home's existing structure, the property lines, zoning setbacks, and whether your foundation can support another story. These aren't questions you can brush past.

Working with a licensed architect based in Westchester, NY means you get someone who will evaluate your specific home and tell you what's actually possible. Some additions work better than others depending on the existing structure, lot size, and neighborhood character. In towns like Pelham, Tuckahoe, and Dobbs Ferry, older homes sometimes need additional foundation work before you can build up.

Once the design is locked in, your contractor guides the project through every phase. The goal is a new second story that functions like it was always part of your home.
